The video segment is a slideshow presentation on the history of the atomic model. The slideshow starts with a slide titled "History of the Atomic Model". The text explains the plum-pudding model of the atom proposed by Joseph John Thomson. The plum-pudding model is illustrated as a pink sphere with yellow circles embedded in it; each circle contains a negative charge symbol. This model is further explained to have negatively charged electrons embedded in a positively charged mass. The slideshow then moves to the Gold Foil Experiment suggested by Ernest Rutherford and conducted by Hans Geiger and Ernest Marsden in 1911. An image of the setup for the Gold Foil Experiment is depicted, showing a source of alpha particles directed at a platinum foil. The slide shows that the experiment was probing the structure of the atom and details expectations, if it was a solid mass or if negative electrons were embedded in a thin positive mass. The slideshow presents results that most alpha particles get through, but some are scattered by the small positive nucleus, leading to Rutherford's model of the atom. The Rutherford model of the atom states that the atom is mostly empty space with a small positive nucleus surrounded by scattered electrons. This led to the planetary model of the atom.
